title.en: Lesson 1. A wish in your heart: -고 싶다

blocks.md:
**-고 싶다** expresses a **wish in your heart**.

Not a locked calendar event, but something you want to do: “I want to…” It pairs naturally with words like “someday” (언젠가), “later” (나중에), or “sometime” (한 번쯤).

blocks.h: Step 1: Drop 다 from the dictionary form
blocks.md:
가**다** → 가
먹**다** → 먹

The part left behind is the **stem**. Every Korean ending attaches here.

blocks.h: Step 2: Attach -고 싶어요 to the stem
blocks.md:
가 + **고 싶어요** → 가고 싶어요
먹 + **고 싶어요** → 먹고 싶어요

No vowel harmony, no 받침 rules: it never changes shape. That makes it one of the friendliest patterns in Korean.

items.tip: I want to go to Jeju someday. / no date set yet
I feel like having something warm and soupy.
I really want to see that film.
I want to live in Korea for about a month.
I want to get better at Korean.

blocks.md:
**Do not use this for other people’s wishes.** When someone else wants to do something, use **-고 싶어하다**:

동생이 가고 싶**어해요**. (○)
동생이 가고 싶어요. (✕)

Korean avoids stating another person’s inner feelings directly, it steps back and says “they appear to want to”.

blocks.h: When to use and when not to use
blocks.md:
**Use it**: when you haven’t decided, but your heart leans that way:
오늘 좀 쉬**고 싶어요**. (I want to rest today.)

**Don’t use it**, for confirmed schedules. That’s -(으)ㄹ 거예요:
세 시에 출발하고 싶어요. (✕ Sounds like a wish when you already have an appointment)
세 시에 출발**할 거예요**. (○ I am going to leave at 3.)

**Don’t use it**, for other people’s minds. Switch to -고 싶어하다.

blocks.meaning: I want to travel the world someday.
blocks.why: “나중에” (someday / later) shows nothing is fixed yet, it is purely a wish, so **가고 싶어요**. 갈 거예요 means a plan is set, 가려고 해요 means intending to, and 가기로 했어요 means scheduled/decided.

blocks.meaning: I feel like eating pizza tonight.
blocks.why: If you already ordered it, you would say **먹을 거예요**. Here it’s just a craving in your mind, so **먹고 싶어요**.

blocks.q: 배우다 (to learn) / “한국 요리를 ___ .” Make it a wish: “I want to learn…”
blocks.why: Attach -고 싶어요 directly to the stem 배우. No stem change needed.

blocks.q: Your younger sibling also wants to go. Which one is correct?
blocks.why: When talking about someone else’s wish, use **-고 싶어하다** → 가고 싶어해요.

blocks.say: 저는 언젠가 제주도에 가서 한 달쯤 살고 싶어요.
blocks.rom: jeo-neun eon-jen-ga je-ju-do-e ga-seo han dal-jjeum sal-go sip-eo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud warmly: “Someday I want to go to Jeju and live there for about a month.”

blocks.md:
**-(으)ㄹ 거예요** expresses a **scheduled or confirmed plan**.

Not just a wish, but a locked plan: you bought the ticket, made the appointment, or firmly resolved to do it. It pairs with specific time words like “tomorrow” (내일), “next week” (다음 주), or “at 3:00” (세 시에).

blocks.h: Step 1: Check for a final consonant (받침)
blocks.md:
만나**다** → 만나 … **no 받침**
읽**다** → 읽 … **has 받침** (ㄱ)

This single check determines everything.

blocks.h: Step 2: No 받침 → -ㄹ 거예요 / Has 받침 → -을 거예요
blocks.md:
No 받침 → stem + **ㄹ 거예요**
만나 + ㄹ 거예요 → **만날 거예요**

Has 받침 → stem + **을 거예요**
읽 + 을 거예요 → **읽을 거예요**

items.ch: 내일 오전 열 시에 친구를 만날 거예요.
items.tip: I am meeting a friend at 10 tomorrow. / appointment made

items.ch: 이번 주말에는 집에서 영화를 볼 거예요.
items.tip: I am going to watch films at home this weekend.

items.ch: 올해는 책을 오십 권 읽을 거예요.
items.tip: I am going to read fifty books this year.
I will eat lunch in front of the school.
I am going to live in Seoul from next month.

blocks.md:
**If the stem already ends in ㄹ, do not add 을.**

살다 → 살 거예요 (○) / 살을 거예요 (✕)
만들다 → 만들 거예요 (○)

Because ㄹ is already there, leave it as is.

blocks.h: When to use and when not to use
blocks.md:
**Use it**: when the time is set, tickets are booked, or the plan is firm:
다음 주에 이사**할 거예요**.

**Don’t use it**, when nothing is decided yet. Use -고 싶어요 instead.

**Related patterns**, **-(으)려고 해요** means “planning/thinking of”, and **-기로 했어요** means “decided on”. All three look ahead, but with different levels of firmness.

blocks.meaning: I am going to meet a friend tomorrow at 10 AM.
blocks.why: “내일 10시” (tomorrow at 10) sets an exact appointment → **만날 거예요**. 만났어요 is past tense, 만나고 싶어요 is just a wish, and 만나려고 해요 means thinking of it.

blocks.meaning: I am going to live in Seoul from next month.
blocks.why: “다음 달부터” (from next month) sets a specific timeline. The stem 살 already ends in ㄹ, so it attaches directly: **살 거예요**.

blocks.q: 읽다 (to read) / “올해는 책을 오십 권 ___ .” Conjugate into -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
blocks.why: 읽 has a 받침 (ㄱ), so attach **을 거예요** → 읽을 거예요.

blocks.q: Match each dictionary verb with its -(으)ㄹ 거예요 form.
Build “I am going to meet a friend tomorrow.”

blocks.say: 다음 주 월요일에 서울역에서 기차를 타고 부산에 갈 거예요.
blocks.rom: da-eum ju wol-yo-il-e seoul-yeog-e-seo gi-cha-reul ta-go bu-san-e gal geo-ye-yo
blocks.q: Say it out loud with clear pacing: “Next Monday, I am taking the train from Seoul Station to Busan.”

blocks.md:
**Is it decided, or still just in your heart?**

If the ticket is bought or appointment booked, use **-(으)ㄹ 거예요**. If it’s still just a wish, use **-고 싶어요**. The time word in the sentence almost always gives away the answer.

head: Clue in sentence
Chosen pattern
Example
rows: 내일 · 다음 주 · 세 시에 (specific time)
그냥 마음이 그래요 (just feel like it)

items.tip: Someday I want to go to Europe. / no fixed plan
I am going to Europe next month. / ticket purchased
I want to learn Korean cooking. / wish
I am going to a cooking class on Saturday. / registered

blocks.md:
**Sometimes both are completely natural.**

“주말에 쉬고 싶어요” and “주말에 쉴 거예요” are both valid. The first is a wish (“I want to rest”), and the second is a decision (“I am going to rest”). It’s about **the speaker’s attitude**.

blocks.sentence: 아직 아무것도 안 정했지만 언젠가 유럽에 [가고 싶어요].
blocks.meaning: Nothing is decided yet, but someday I want to go to Europe.
blocks.why: “아직 아무것도 안 정했지만” (nothing is decided yet) is the clue, with no set schedule, it is a wish: **가고 싶어요**.

blocks.sentence: 비행기표를 벌써 샀어요. 다음 달에 유럽에 [갈 거예요].
blocks.meaning: I already bought the ticket. I am going to Europe next month.
blocks.why: The ticket is bought and month is set. It is a scheduled plan, so **갈 거예요**.

blocks.meaning: My friend wants to go study in Korea.
blocks.why: The subject is a friend (third person). For someone else’s desire, use **-고 싶어하다**.

blocks.q: Match each situation with the matching expression.
pairs: A scheduled plan with a date

blocks.say: 지금은 그냥 가고 싶은 마음이지만, 돈을 모으면 내년에는 꼭 갈 거예요.
blocks.rom: ji-geum-eun geu-nyang ga-go sip-eun ma-eum-i-ji-man, don-eul mo-eu-myeon nae-nyeon-e-neun kkok gal geo-ye-yo
blocks.q: First half is a wish, second half is a firm plan: “Right now it is just a wish, but when I save money, I will definitely go next year.”

title.en: Lesson 4. Conjugation Forms by Batchim and Irregulars

blocks.h: How Stems Attach to -고 싶다 and -(으)ㄹ 거예요
blocks.md:
Let's compare the attachment rules side by side:

- **-고 싶어요 (Desire):** Super simple! Just attach **-고 싶어요** directly to any verb stem. No exceptions, no changes!
- **-(으)ㄹ 거예요 (Future plan):** Depends on 받침:
  - **No 받침:** attach **-ㄹ 거예요** (가다 → **갈 거예요**).
  - **With 받침:** attach **-을 거예요** (먹다 → **먹을 거예요**).
  - **ㄹ stem:** merges into **-ㄹ 거예요** (만들다 → **만들 거예요**).
  - **ㄷ irregular:** ㄷ changes to ㄹ (듣다 → **들을 거예요**).
Look at **듣다**! For desire, it's **듣고 싶어요** (no change before ㄱ). For future plan, it's **들을 거예요** (ㄷ softens to ㄹ before 으).

items.tip: I want to listen to a lot of Korean music. (듣다 + 고 싶어요)
I will listen to music at the concert tomorrow. (듣다 + 을 거예요)
I will make a cake on the weekend. (만들다 + ㄹ 거예요)

blocks.q: How do you form the future plan for ‘만들다’ (to make)?
blocks.why: Stems ending in ㄹ attach - 거예요 directly, so 만들다 becomes **만들 거예요**.

blocks.q: Which is the correct future plan form of ‘듣다’ (to listen)?
blocks.why: 듣다 changes ㄷ to ㄹ before vowel endings: 듣 + 을 거예요 → **들을 거예요**.

blocks.q: Match each verb to its correct -(으)ㄹ 거예요 form.

blocks.sentence: 내일 친구와 함께 맛있는 점심을 [먹을 거예요].
blocks.meaning: Tomorrow I will eat a delicious lunch with a friend.
blocks.why: 먹다 has a final consonant (ㄱ), so it attaches -을 거예요 → **먹을 거예요**.

blocks.q: Conjugate 돕다 (to help) into the future plan form -(으)ㄹ 거예요: 「제가 친구를 ___ .」
blocks.why: 돕다 changes ㅂ to 우 before vowels: 도우 + ㄹ 거예요 → **도울 거예요**.

blocks.say: 주말에 친구를 만나서 맛있는 음식을 먹고 쇼핑할 거예요.
blocks.rom: ju-mal-e chin-gu-reul man-na-seo mas-iss-neun eum-sig-eul meog-go syo-ping-hal geo-ye-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud expressing a weekend plan clearly.
